name: Release Obsidian theme
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "*"
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check the tag matches manifest.json
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}"
          version="$(jq -r '.version' manifest.json)"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag '$tag' does not match the version '$version' in manifest.json." >&2
            echo "Obsidian expects the release tag to be the bare version number, with no 'v' prefix." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Generate artifact attestation
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            theme.css
            manifest.json

      - name: Create release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}"
          gh release create "$tag" \
            --title="$tag" \
            --generate-notes \
            --draft \
            theme.css manifest.json

# Kanagawa Tide

![Kanagawa Tide, dark and light side by side](images/cover.webp)

An Obsidian theme built on two Kanagawa palettes: Wave for the deep sumi-ink night of dark mode, Neutral Light for the warm neutral paper of light mode. Both descend from [rebelot/kanagawa.nvim](https://github.com/rebelot/kanagawa.nvim), inspired by Katsushika Hokusai's *The Great Wave off Kanagawa*.

Every colour is picked deliberately in each mode, contrast checked and tuned for long writing sessions rather than screenshots. Spacing gets the same treatment: margins, padding and rhythm are revised throughout so the whole thing feels calm to work in.

## Preview

**Dark mode: Wave**

![Kanagawa Tide in dark mode](images/dark.webp)

**Light mode: Neutral Light**

![Kanagawa Tide in light mode](images/light.webp)

## Install

**Manually**

1. Copy this folder into `<your vault>/.obsidian/themes/Kanagawa Tide/` (the folder name must match the `name` in `manifest.json`).
2. Obsidian → Settings → Appearance → Themes → **Kanagawa Tide**.

**With [BRAT](https://github.com/TfTHacker/obsidian42-brat)**

Add the repository through *Add beta theme*.

Dark and light mode both come from this one theme. Switch with Settings → Appearance → Base color scheme.

## Style Settings

Optional, via the [Style Settings](https://github.com/mgmeyers/obsidian-style-settings) plugin.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Heading colours | Monochrome (default), the single colour each palette defines for headings, or a Kanagawa hue scale across H1–H6 |
| Extra bold H1–H3 | Heavier weight for the top three levels |
| Plain bold and italic | Removes the tint on `**bold**` and `*italic*` |
| Highlight the active line | Subtle background behind the cursor's line |
| Hide the accent bar on the active tab | Removes the 2px accent underline |
| Chrome depth | Flat in dark and layered in light (default), flat in both, or layered in both |

## Accent colour

Leaving Settings → Appearance → **Accent color** on *Default* is the recommended setting: the theme then picks a hue per mode, crystalBlue `#7E9CD8` in dark and `#8692CB` in light, instead of forcing one value onto two very different backgrounds. Against its own background the dark accent measures 5.9:1 and the light one 2.8:1, a quieter periwinkle that keeps the chrome calm on paper.

Obsidian's picker is a single global value shared by both modes, so a custom accent is always a compromise: no hue clears AA on both `#1F1F28` and `#F5F5F2`. If you want one anyway, these are the balanced Kanagawa choices:

| Accent | Hex | On dark | On light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dragonBlue | `#658594` | 4.2:1 | 3.6:1 |
| waveAqua1 | `#6A9589` | 4.9:1 | 3.1:1 |
| oniViolet | `#957FB8` | 4.7:1 | 3.2:1 |

All three clear the 3:1 threshold for non-text UI in both modes, which is what the accent is mostly used for here: tab bar, cursor, checkboxes, focus rings, buttons. In light mode all three also read stronger than the default periwinkle, so this is the route to take if you want the accent to carry more weight on paper. Anything lighter (carpYellow, surimiOrange, springGreen) is dark-mode only; anything darker (`#345E9D`, `#2A7081`) is light-mode only.

Whatever you pick drives every accented surface, and label text on accented buttons and badges flips between black and white automatically based on the accent's perceptual lightness. Links keep their palette colour on purpose (crystalBlue in dark, `#345E9D` in light, matching the source themes), so they stay readable regardless of the accent. Only their hover state follows it. To make the resting colour follow it too, add `.theme-dark, .theme-light { --kt-link: var(--kt-accent); }` to a CSS snippet. The selector matters: `--kt-link` is defined on `.theme-dark` and `.theme-light`, so a snippet targeting `:root` or bare `body` loses to it.

blank_issues_enabled: false
contact_links:
  - name: Obsidian Discord
    url: https://discord.gg/obsidianmd
    about: General questions about themes, snippets and appearance
  - name: Obsidian theme documentation
    url: https://help.obsidian.md/Extending+Obsidian/Themes
    about: How themes, CSS variables and snippets work in Obsidian
  - name: Kanagawa palette
    url: https://github.com/rebelot/kanagawa.nvim
    about: The upstream palettes this theme is built on

name: Bug report
description: Report something that looks wrong in Kanagawa Tide
labels: ["bug"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thanks for taking the time to fill this out. The more of it you complete, the faster the fix.
  - type: dropdown
    id: default-theme
    attributes:
      label: Is the bug present when using the default Obsidian theme?
      description: Switch to the default theme to check whether this is a theme issue or an Obsidian one.
      options:
        - "No"
        - "Yes"
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: dropdown
    id: plugins-disabled
    attributes:
      label: Is the bug present with community plugins and CSS snippets disabled?
      description: Disable snippets and plugins that could be styling the same elements.
      options:
        - "No"
        - "Yes"
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: dropdown
    id: color-scheme
    attributes:
      label: Which colour scheme?
      description: Settings > Appearance > Base color scheme
      options:
        - Dark (Wave)
        - Light (Neutral Light)
        - Both
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: Kanagawa Tide version
      description: Found in Settings > Appearance > Manage. Please update to the latest version before reporting.
      placeholder: e.g. 1.0.0
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: accent
    attributes:
      label: Accent colour
      description: Settings > Appearance > Accent color. Write "Default" if you have not changed it.
      placeholder: Default
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: style-settings
    attributes:
      label: Style Settings changed from their defaults
      description: If you use the Style Settings plugin, list the options you changed under Kanagawa Tide.
      placeholder: e.g. Heading colours set to Kanagawa hue scale, Chrome depth set to flat in both
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: description
    attributes:
      label: Describe the bug
      description: What you expected, what happened instead, and the steps to reproduce it. Screenshots help a lot for visual bugs.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: debug-info
    attributes:
      label: Debug info
      description: In Obsidian press Ctrl/Cmd-P, run `Show debug info`, then `Copy to clipboard` and paste it here.
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true
